children.text: dukūlaṃ bibhrāṇo dalitaharitāladyutiharaṃ javāpuṣpaśreṇīrucirucirapādāmbujatalaḥ
children.translated_text: May there shine in my heart that certain person, wearing a silk garment that steals the splendor of split orpiment, the soles of whose lotus feet are lovely with the hue of rows of hibiscus flowers,

children.text: tamālaśyāmāṅgo darahasitalīlāñchitamukhaḥ parānandābhogaḥ sphuratu hṛdi me kopipuruṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whose limbs are dark like a tamāla tree, whose face is marked by the play of a gentle smile, an expanse of supreme bliss.

children.text: yadā yāto gopīhṛdayamadano nandasadanān mukundo gāndhinyās tanayam anuvindan madhupurīm
children.translated_text: When <s>Mukunda</s>, the love-god of the gopīs’ hearts, went from <s>Nanda</s>’s house to the city of <s>Madhu</s>, seeking the son of <s>Gāndhinī</s>,

children.text: tadāmāṅkṣīc cintāsariti ghanaghūrṇaparicayair agādhāyāṃ bādhāmayapayasi rādhā virahiṇī ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Rādhā</s>, separated from her beloved, plunged into the river of anxiety, into its unfathomable, pain-filled water, familiar with dense whirlings.

children.text: kadācit khedāgniṃ vighaṭayitum antargatam asau sahālībhirlebhe taralitamanā yāmunataṭīm
children.translated_text: Once, wishing to disperse the fire of grief within her, she, her mind unsteady, reached the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s> together with her friends.

children.text: cirādasyāścittaṃ paricitakuṭīrāvakalanād avasthāṃ tastāra sphūṭamatha suṣupteḥ priyasakhīm ||
children.translated_text: After a long time, from seeing the familiar bowers, her mind clearly passed into a condition akin to deep sleep.

children.text: tadā niṣpandāṅgī kalitanalinīpallavakulaiḥ parīṇāhāt premnāmakuśalaśatāśaṅkihṛdayaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, as her limbs lay motionless, her attendants, their hearts fearing hundreds of misfortunes born from the fullness of her love, gathered clusters of lotus shoots;

children.text: dṛgambhogambhīrīkṛtamihiraputrīlaharibhir vilīnā dhūlināmupari parivavre parijanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, while the waves of the daughter of the Sun were deepened by the water of their eyes, they covered her as she lay dissolved upon the dust.

children.text: tatastāṃ nyastāṅgīmurasi lalitāyāḥ kamalinīpalāśaiḥ kālindīsalilaśiśirairvījitatanum
children.translated_text: Then, as she rested with her body placed on <s>Lalitā</s>’s breast, her body fanned with lotus petals cooled by the waters of the <s>Kālindī</s>,

children.text: parāvṛttaśvāsāṅkuracalitakaṇṭhīṃ kalayatāṃ sakhīsaṃdohānāṃ pramadabharaśālī dhvanirabhūt ||
children.translated_text: and as her throat trembled with the first stirrings of returning breath, a sound arose from the gathered friends, full of delight.

children.text: nidhāyāṅke paṅkeruhadalaviṭaṅkasya lalitā tato rādhāṃ nīrāharaṇasaraṇīnyastacaraṇā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Lalitā</s>, having laid <s>Rādhā</s> in the lap formed by the rim of a lotus leaf, set her feet on the path for bringing water.

children.text: milantaṃ kālindīpulinabhuvi khelāñcitagatiṃ dadarśāgre kaṃcinmadhuravirutaṃ śvetagarutam ||
children.translated_text: Before her, on the sandy bank of the <s>Kālindī</s>, she saw a certain white-winged bird coming near, moving with playful gait and uttering a sweet cry.

children.text: tadālokastokocchvasitahṛdayā sādaramasau praṇāmaṃ saṃśantī laghu laghu samāsādya savidham
children.translated_text: At the sight of it her heart breathed a little again; approaching it quickly and respectfully, and offering a reverent salutation,

children.text: dhṛtotkaṇṭhā sadyo harisadasi saṃdeśaharaṇe varaṃ dūtaṃ mene tam atilalitaṃ hanta lalitā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>, seized at once by longing, thought that very graceful bird the best messenger for carrying a message to <s>Hari</s>’s abode.

children.text: amarṣāt premerṣyāṃ sapadi dadhatī kaṃsamathane pravṛttā haṃsāya khamabhilaṣitaṃ śaṃsitumasau
children.translated_text: Out of impatience, instantly holding love-jealousy toward the slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, she began to tell the swan what she wished for:

children.text: na tasyā doṣo'yaṃ yadiha vihagaṃ prārthitavatī na kasmin visrambhaṃ diśati haribhaktipraṇayitā ||
children.translated_text: It is no fault of hers if she has entreated a bird here; affection for <s>Hari</s>’s devotees places trust in everyone.

children.text: pavitreṣu prāyo viracayasi toyeṣu vasatiṃ pramodaṃ nālīke vahasi viśadātmā svayamasi
children.translated_text: You generally make your dwelling in pure waters; you take delight in lotuses; you yourself are of a clear nature.

children.text: ato'haṃ duḥkhārtā śaraṇam avalā tvāṃ gatavatī na bhikṣā satpakṣe vrajati hi kadācid viphalatām ||
children.translated_text: Therefore I, distressed by sorrow and helpless, have come to you for refuge. A request made to one with good wings, to a worthy side, never proves fruitless.

children.text: ciraṃ vismṛtyāsmān virahadahanajvālavikalāḥ kalāvān sānandaṃ vasati mathurāyāṃ madhuripuḥ
children.translated_text: For a long time the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>, forgetting us who are distraught with the flame of the fire of separation, has been living happily in <s>Mathurā</s>, full of arts.

children.text: tadetaṃ saṃdeśaṃ svamanasi samādhāya nikhila bhavān kṣipraṃ tasya śravaṇapadavīṃ saṃgamayatu ||
children.translated_text: So, fixing this whole message in your own mind, may you quickly bring it onto the path of his hearing.

children.text: nirastapratyūhaṃ bhavatu bhavato vartmani śivaṃ samuttiṣṭha kṣipraṃ manasi mudamādhāya sadayam
children.translated_text: May there be good fortune on your road, free from obstacles. Rise up quickly, placing gladness and compassion in your mind.

children.text: adhastāddhāvanto laghu laghu samuttānanayanair bhavantaṃ vīkṣantāṃ kutukataralā gopaśiśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let the cowherd boys running below you quickly look up with uplifted eyes, watching you with trembling curiosity.

children.text: kiśorottaṃśo 'sau kaṭhinamatinā dānapatinā yayā ninye tūrṇaṃ paśupayuvatījīvitapatiḥ
children.translated_text: By the very road by which that crest-jewel of youths, the lord of the lives of the cowherd girls, was swiftly taken by the hard-hearted lord of gifts,

children.text: tayā gantavyā te nikhilajagadekaprathitayā padavyā bhavyānāṃ tilaka kila dāśārhanagarī ||
children.translated_text: by that road, famous as the one path of the whole world, you must go, O ornament of the noble, to the city of the <s>Dāśārhas</s>.

children.text: galadbāṣpāsāraplutadhavalagaṇḍā mṛgadṛśo vidūyante yatra prabalamadanā veśavivaśāḥ
children.translated_text: Where doe-eyed women, their white cheeks flooded with streams of falling tears, are tormented, overwhelmed in their dress by powerful passion,

children.text: tvayā vijñātavyā haricaraṇasaṅgapraṇayino dhruvaṃ sā cakrāṅgī ratisakhaśatāṅgasya padavī ||
children.translated_text: there you should know for certain the track of the chariot of love’s friend, marked with wheels and dear because of its contact with <s>Hari</s>’s feet.

children.text: piban jambuśyāmaṃ mihiraduhitar vāri madhuraṃ mṛṇālīr bhuñjāno himakarakalākomalarucaḥ
children.translated_text: Drinking the sweet, rose-apple-dark water of the daughter of the Sun, and eating lotus fibers tender and bright like digits of the moon,

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ hṛṣṭastiṣṭhan nibiḍaviṭape śākhini sakhe sukhena prasthānaṃ racayatu bhavān vṛṣṇinagare ||
children.translated_text: stay delighted for a moment, friend, in a tree with dense branches; then may you comfortably set out toward the city of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>.

children.text: balād ākrandan tīrthapathikam akrūramilitaṃ vidūrādābhīrītatīranuyayau yena ramaṇam
children.translated_text: The path by which he, crying out forcefully, followed from afar his beloved, who had met <s>Akrūra</s>, while the women of the cowherd settlement followed along the bank,

children.text: tamādau panthānaṃ racaya caritārthā bhavatu te virājantī sarvopari paramahaṃsasthitiriyam ||
children.translated_text: make that your first road. May this state of yours as a supreme swan, shining above all, become fulfilled.

children.text: akasmādasmākaṃ harirapaharannaṃśukacayaṃ yamārūḍho gūḍhapraṇayalaharīṃ kandalayitum
children.translated_text: The kadamba tree on which <s>Hari</s> suddenly climbed, stealing our heap of garments in order to make the hidden waves of love sprout forth,

children.text: tava śrāntasyāntaḥsthagitaravibimbaḥ kisalayaiḥ kadambaḥ kādamba tvaritamavalambaḥ sa bhavitā ||
children.translated_text: that kadamba, O water-bird, with the sun’s disk concealed within by its young leaves, will quickly become a support for you when you are weary.

children.text: kirantī lāvaṇyaṃ diśi diśi śikhaṇḍastavakinī dadhānā sādhīyaḥ kanakavimaladyotivasanam
children.translated_text: Scattering beauty in every direction, bearing a cluster of peacock plumes, wearing a garment whose radiance is exceedingly pure like gold,

children.text: tamālaśyāmāṅgī saralamuralīcumbitamukhī jagau citraṃ yatra prakaṭaparamānandalaharī ||
children.translated_text: dark-limbed like a tamāla tree, her face kissed by the straight flute, she sang there wondrously, a manifest wave of supreme bliss.

children.text: tayā bhūyaḥ krīḍārabhasavikasadvallabhavadhū vapurvallībhraśyanmṛgamadakaṇaśyāmalikayā
children.translated_text: Again, by that place of the rāsa dance, darkened by particles of musk slipping from the vine-like bodies of the beloved women as they blossomed in the excitement of play,

children.text: vidhātavyo hallīsakadalitamallīlatikayā samantādullāsastava manasi rāsasthalikayā ||
children.translated_text: and with jasmine creepers crushed by the hallīsa dance, an all-around exultation should be produced in your mind.

children.text: tadante vāsantīviracitam anaṅgotsavakalācatuḥśālaṃ śaureḥ sphurati na dṛśau tatra vikireḥ
children.translated_text: Beyond that shines the four-sided pavilion for the festival arts of <s>Anaṅga</s>, made by <s>Vāsantī</s> for <s>Śauri</s>; do not cast your eyes there.

children.text: tadālokodbhedapramadabharavismāritagatikriye jāne tāvattvayi bata hatā gopavanitā ||
children.translated_text: For, your motion and action forgotten through the joy and astonishment born from seeing it, I think then, alas, that the cowherd women will have been ruined in regard to you.

children.text: mama syādarthānāṃ kṣatiriha vilambādyadapi te vilokethāḥ sarvaṃ tadapi harikelisthalamidam
children.translated_text: Although my purposes may suffer loss here through your delay, still you should look at all this place of <s>Hari</s>’s play.

children.text: taveyaṃ na vyarthā bhavatu śucitā kaḥ sa hi sakhe guṇo yaśvāṇūradviṣi matiniveśāya na bhavet ||
children.translated_text: May this purity of yours not be in vain; for what virtue, friend, would not lead to fixing the mind on the enemy of <s>Cāṇūra</s>?

children.text: sakṛdvaṃśīnādaśravaṇamilitābhīravanitā rahaḥkrīḍāsākṣī pratipadalatāsadmasubhagaḥ
children.translated_text: Your <s>Govardhana</s> mountain, friend of the cows, whose rocks have been made into couches by the slayer of <s>Madhu</s>, is beautiful with bowers of vines at every step, witnesses to the secret sports of the cowherd women gathered by hearing even once the sound of the flute.

children.text: sa dhenūnāṃ bandhur madhumathanakhaṭvāyitaśilaḥ kariṣyatyānandaṃ sapadi tava govardhanagiriḥ ||
children.translated_text: That <s>Govardhana</s> mountain will at once give you delight.

children.text: tamevādriṃ cakrāṅkitakarapariṣvaṅgarasikaṃ mahīcakre śaṅkemahi śikhariṇāṃ śekharatayā
children.translated_text: We think that very mountain, fond of the embrace of the hand marked with the discus, is the crest-jewel of mountains upon the circle of the earth.

children.text: arātiṃ jñātīnāṃ nanu harihayaṃ yaḥ paribhavan yathārthaṃ svaṃ nāma vyadhita bhuvi govardhana iti ||
children.translated_text: For, defeating <s>Indra</s>, the enemy of his kinsmen, he made his own name, <s>Govardhana</s>, truly meaningful upon the earth.

children.text: tamālasyālokādgiriparisare santi capalāḥ pulindo govindasmaraṇarabhasottaptavapuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: At the sight of tamāla trees near the mountain there are restless <s>Pulinda</s> women, their bodies heated by the impetuous remembrance of <s>Govinda</s>.

children.text: śanaistāpaṃ tāsāṃ kṣaṇamapanayan yāsyati bhavān avaśyaṃ kālindīsalilaśiśiraiḥ pakṣapavanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: You will surely pass along, slowly removing their fever for a moment with wing-breezes cooled by the waters of the <s>Kālindī</s>.

children.text: tadante śrīkāntasmarasamaradhāṭīpuṭakitā kadambānāṃ vāṭī rasikaparipāṭīṃ sphuṭayati
children.translated_text: At its end a grove of kadamba trees, bristling from the battle-array of desire for the beloved of <s>Śrī</s>, makes manifest the tradition of connoisseurs.

children.text: tvamāsīnastasyāṃ na yadi parito nandasi tato babhūva vyarthā te ghanarasaniveśavyasanitā ||
children.translated_text: If, seated there, you do not rejoice all around, then your passion for dwelling in the dense essence has been in vain.

children.text: śaranmeghaśreṇīpratibhaṭam ariṣṭāsuraśiraś ciraṃ śuṣkaṃ vṛndāvanaparisare drakṣyati bhavān
children.translated_text: In the region of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> you will see the long-dried head of the demon <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, a rival to a row of autumn clouds.

children.text: yadāroḍhuṃ dūrānmilati kila kailāsaśikharibhramākrāntasvānto giriśasuhṛdaḥ kiṃkaragaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: To climb it, they say, the servants of <s>Śiva</s>'s friend gather from afar, their minds seized by the illusion that it is the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>.

children.text: ruvan yāhi svairaṃ caramadaśayā cumbitaruco nitambinyo vṛndāvanabhuvi sakhe santi bahavaḥ
children.translated_text: Crying out, go freely, friend; on the land of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> there are many shapely women whose beauty is kissed by the final condition.

children.text: parāvartiṣyante tulitamurajinnūpuraravāt tava dhvānāttāsāṃ bahirapi gatāḥ kṣipramasavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From your call, measured against the sound of the anklets of the slayer of <s>Mura</s>, even their life-breaths, though gone outside, will quickly turn back.

children.text: tvamāsīnaḥ śākhāntaramilitacaṇḍatviṣi sukhaṃ dadhīthā bhāṇḍīre kṣaṇamapi ghanaśyāmalarucau
children.translated_text: Seated at ease in <s>Bhāṇḍīra</s>, dark as a cloud, where the fierce-rayed sun is caught among the branches, you should rest even for a moment.

children.text: tato haṃsā bibhrannikhilanabhasaś cikramiṣayā sa vardhiṣṇuṃ viṣṇuṃ kalitadaracakraṃ tulayitā ||
children.translated_text: Then, O swan, as if wishing to traverse the whole sky, it will resemble the growing <s>Viṣṇu</s> bearing the conch and discus.

children.text: tvam aṣṭābhir netrair vigaladamalapremasalilair muhuḥ siktastambhāṃ catura caturāsyastutibhuvam
children.translated_text: Clever one, you should abandon the famous ground praised by four-faced <s>Brahmā</s>, whose pillars are again and again sprinkled by streams of pure tears of love flowing from his eight eyes.

children.text: jihīthā vikhyātāṃ sphuṭamiha bhavadbāndhavarathaṃ praviṣṭaṃ maṃsyante vidhim aṭavidevyas tvayi gate ||
children.translated_text: When you have gone there, the forest goddesses will think that <s>Brahmā</s>, your kinsman's vehicle, has clearly entered it here.

children.text: udañchannetrāmbhaḥ prasaralaharīpicchilapathaskhalatpādanyāsapraṇihitavilambākuladhiyaḥ
children.translated_text: In that place, when <s>Hari</s> plunged in, the gopīs, their minds confused by delay as their placed footsteps slipped on the path made slimy by waves of rising tears from their eyes, were seized by the desire to go quickly to the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>.

children.text: harau yasminmagne tvaritayamunākūlagamanaspṛhākṣiptā gopyo yayuranupadaṃ kāmapi daśām ||
children.translated_text: They reached some indescribable state, following after him step by step.

children.text: muhurlāsyakrīḍāpramadamiladāhopuruṣikā vikāśena bhraṣṭaiḥ phaṇimaṇikuler dhūmalarucau
children.translated_text: Before that holy <s>Kāliya</s> pool, dark with the smoky luster of heaps of serpent-jewels fallen through the expansion of the joy of repeated dancing sports and the encounter with exclamations of wonder,

children.text: puras tasmin nīpadrumakusumakiñjalkasurabhau tvayā puṇye peyaṃ madhuramudakaṃ kāliyahrade ||
children.translated_text: and fragrant with the pollen of nīpa-tree flowers, you should drink the sweet water.

children.text: tṛṇāvartārāter virahadavasaṃtāpitatanoḥ sadābhīrīvṛndapraṇayabahumānonnatividaḥ
children.translated_text: To <s>Vṛndādevī</s>, whose body is scorched by the forest fire of separation from the enemy of <s>Tṛṇāvarta</s>, and who always knows the exalted affection and honor of the cowherd women,

children.text: praṇetavyo navyastabakabharasaṃvardhitaśucas tvayā vṛndādevyāḥ paramavinayādvandanavidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: you should offer with the utmost humility a new rite of salutation, whose purity is increased by the burden of fresh clusters of blossoms.

children.text: iti krāntvā kekākṛtavirutim ekādaśavanīṃ ghanībhūtaṃ cūtair vrajam anuvanaṃ dvādaśamidam
children.translated_text: Having thus passed the eleventh wood, resonant with peacock-like cries, and then this twelfth wood of <s>Vraja</s>, dense with mango trees, grove after grove,

children.text: purī yasminnāste yadukulabhuvāṃ nirmalayaśo bharāṇāṃ dhārābhir dhavalitadharitrīparisarā ||
children.translated_text: there stands the city in which the surrounding earth is whitened by streams of the pure fame borne by those born in the <s>Yadu</s> line.

children.text: niketairākīrṇā giriśagiriḍimbhapratibhaṭair avaṣṭambhastambhāvalivilasitaiḥ puṣpitavanā
children.translated_text: Crowded with houses rivaling the young peaks of <s>Śiva</s>'s mountain, shining with rows of supporting pillars, and rich with flowering groves,

children.text: niviṣṭā kālindītaṭabhuvi tavādhāsyati sakhe samantādānandaṃ madhurajanavṛndā madhupurī ||
children.translated_text: the city of <s>Madhupurī</s>, settled on the bank of the <s>Kālindī</s> and filled with pleasant people, will give you delight on every side, friend.

children.text: vṛṣaḥ śambhoryasyāṃ daśati navamekatra yavasaṃ viriñcer anyasmin gilati kalahaṃso bisalatām
children.translated_text: In that city, in one place <s>Śiva</s>'s bull bites fresh grass, and in another <s>Brahmā</s>'s royal swan swallows lotus fibers.

children.text: kvacit krauñcārāteḥ kavalayati kekī viṣadharaṃ vilīḍhe śallakyā balaripukarī pallavamitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Somewhere the peacock of the enemy of <s>Krauñca</s> devours a snake, and elsewhere the elephant of the enemy of <s>Bala</s> licks a tender shoot of śallakī.

children.text: avodhiṣṭhāḥ kāṣān nahi vighaṭitāṃ pracchadapaṭīṃ vimuktāmajñāsīḥ pathi pathi na muktāvalimapi
children.translated_text: You did not notice your saffron garments; you did not know that your covering cloth was disordered; on every road you did not notice even your freed pearl necklace.

children.text: ayi śrīgovindasmaraṇamadirāmattahṛdaye satīti khyātiṃ te hasati kulaṭānāṃ kulamidam ||
children.translated_text: O you whose heart is drunk with the wine of remembering blessed <s>Govinda</s>, this whole clan of unchaste women laughs at your reputation as a faithful wife.

children.text: asavyaṃ bibhrāṇā padamadhṛtalākṣārasamasau prayātāhaṃ mugdhe virama mama veśaiḥ kimadhunā
children.translated_text: I have set down the left foot without holding lac-dye; I have set out, foolish girl. Stop. What now is the use of my adornments?

children.text: amandād āśaṅke sakhi purapuraṃdhrīkalakalād alindāgre vṛndāvanakusumadhanvā vijayate ||
children.translated_text: Friend, from the loud tumult of the city women I strongly suspect that the flower-bowed god of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> is triumphant at the front of the balcony.

children.text: ayaṃ līlāpāṅgasnapitapuravīthīparisaro navāśokottaṃsaścalati purataḥ kaṃsavijayī
children.translated_text: This conqueror of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, with the region of the city streets bathed by his playful side-glances and with a fresh aśoka crest-ornament, moves before us.

children.text: kim asmān etasmānmaṇibhavanapṛṣṭhād vinudatī tvamekā stabdhākṣi sthagayasi gavākṣāvalimapi ||
children.translated_text: Why, driving us away from the roof of this jeweled mansion, do you alone, O fixed-eyed one, block even the row of windows?

children.text: muhuḥ śūnyāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ vahasi rahasi dhyāyasi sadā śṛṇoṣi pratyakṣaṃ na parijanavijñāpanaśatam
children.translated_text: Again and again you bear an empty gaze; in secret you are always meditating; you do not directly hear even hundreds of messages from your attendants.

children.text: ataḥ śaṅke paṅkeruhamukhi yayau śyāmalaruciḥ sa yūnām uttuṃsastava nayanavīthīpathikatām ||
children.translated_text: Therefore I suspect, lotus-faced one, that he of dark radiance, the crest-ornament of young men, has become a traveler on the road of your eyes.

children.text: vilajjaṃ mā rodīr iha sakhi punaryāsyati haris tavāpāṅgakrīḍānibiḍaparicaryāgrahilatām
children.translated_text: Do not weep shamelessly here, friend; <s>Hari</s> will come again to the dense service-vine seized by the play of your sidelong glances.

children.text: iti khairaṃ yasyāṃ pathi pathi murārer abhinavapraveśe nārīṇāṃ ratirabhasajalpā vavanire ||
children.translated_text: Thus, at every road in that city, on the fresh entrance of the enemy of <s>Mura</s>, new love-impelled chatter of women was uttered.

children.text: pañcabhiḥ kulakam
children.translated_text: A group of five verses.

children.text: sakhe sākṣāddāmodaravadanacandrā vakalanasphuratatpremānandaprakaralaharīcumbitadhiyaḥ
children.translated_text: Friend, there the city women, their minds kissed by billows of manifest supreme bliss as they behold the moon-face of <s>Dāmodara</s> directly,

children.text: muhus tatrābhīrīsamudayaśironyastavipadas tavākṣṇor ānandaṃ vidadhati purā pauravanitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: again and again place upon your eyes a joy whose calamity rests on the heads of the gathered cowherd women.

children.text: atha krāmaṃ krāmaṃ kramaghaṭanayā saṃkaṭatarān nivāsān vṛṣṇīnām anusara purīmadhyaviśikhān
children.translated_text: Then, step by step, in due sequence, follow through the lanes in the middle of the city the ever more crowded dwellings of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>.

children.text: murārāteryatra sthagitagaganābhir vijayate patākābhiḥ saṃtarpitabhuvanam antaḥpuravaram ||
children.translated_text: There the excellent inner palace of <s>Murāri</s> triumphs, satisfying the worlds with banners that seem to block the sky.

children.text: yadutsaṅge tuṅgasphaṭikaracitāḥ santi parito marālā māṇikyaprakaraghaṭitatroṭicaraṇāḥ
children.translated_text: In its courtyard, all around, are swans made of lofty crystal, their beaks and feet fashioned from clusters of rubies.

children.text: suhṛdbuddhyā haṃsāḥ kalitamadhurasyāmbujabhuvaḥ samaryādā yeṣāṃ sapadi paricaryāṃ vidadhati ||
children.translated_text: Thinking them friends, the swans of sweetly fashioned speech, born from the lotus-born god, at once perform due service to them.

children.text: cirān mṛgyantīnāṃ paśuparamaṇīnāmapi kulair alabdhaṃ kālindīpulinavipine līnamabhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Long sought even by herds of lovely cows, yet not obtained, hidden all about in the forest on the bank of the <s>Kālindī</s>,

children.text: madālokollāsismitaparicitāsyaṃ priyasakṣi sphurantaṃ vīkṣiṣye punarapi kimagre murabhidam ||
children.translated_text: O dear witness, shall I once more see before me <s>Murabhid</s>, his face made familiar by a smile brightened at the sight of me?

children.text: viṣādaṃ mākārṣīrdrutam avitathavyāhṛtirasau samāgantā rādhe dhṛtanavaśikhaṇḍastava sakhā
children.translated_text: Do not give way to sorrow. That true-speaking friend of yours, wearing a fresh peacock plume, will quickly come, O <s>Rādhā</s>.

children.text: iti brūte yasyāṃ śukamithunamindrānuja kṛte yadābhīrīvṛndairupahṛtamabhūduddhavakare ||
children.translated_text: So speaks, in that place, a pair of parrots for the sake of the younger brother of <s>Indra</s>, when he had been offered into <s>Uddhava</s>'s hand by the groups of cowherd women.

children.text: ghanaśyāmā bhrāmyatyupari hariharmyasya śikhibhiḥ kṛtastotrā mugdhairagurujanitā dhūmalatikā
children.translated_text: Above <s>Hari</s>'s palace wanders a dark cloud: a curling thread of smoke born from aloe, praised by innocent peacocks.

children.text: tadālokād dhīra sphurati tava cenmānasarucir jitaṃ tarhi svairaṃ janasahanivāsapriyatayā ||
children.translated_text: If, steady one, your heart's delight stirs at the sight of it, then you have freely been conquered by love of dwelling together with people.

children.text: tato madhye kakṣaṃ pratinavagavākṣastavakitaṃ calanmuktālambasphuritam amalastambhanivaham
children.translated_text: Then, in the middle court, studded with ever-new windows and gleaming with swinging pearl pendants, with rows of spotless pillars,

children.text: bhavān draṣṭā hemollikhitadaśamaskandhacaritair lasadbhittiprāntaṃ muravijayinaḥ kelinilayam ||
children.translated_text: you will see the play-abode of the conqueror of <s>Mura</s>, its shining wall-edges inscribed in gold with the deeds of the Tenth Book.

children.text: alinde yasyāste marakatamayī yaṣṭiramalā śayāluryāṃ rātrau madakalakalāpī kalayati
children.translated_text: On its balcony stands a spotless emerald perch, upon which at night a drunkenly sweet-voiced peacock lies down and sings.

children.text: nirātaṅkaṃ tasyāḥ śikharamadhiruhya śramanudaṃ pratīkṣethā bhrātarvaramavasaraṃ yādavapateḥ ||
children.translated_text: Climb its summit without fear, brother, and, easing your fatigue, wait for the excellent opportunity of the lord of the <s>Yādavas</s>.

children.text: niviṣṭaḥ palyaṅke mṛdulataratūlīdhavalite trilokīlakṣmīṇāṃ kakudi darasācīkṛtatanuḥ
children.translated_text: Seated on a couch whitened by very soft cotton, his body slightly bent upon the peak of the fortune of the three worlds,

children.text: amandaṃ pūrṇendupratimamupadhānaṃ pramudito nidhāyāgre tasminn upahitakapholidvayabharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: joyfully placing before him a pillow like the full moon, with the weight of both cheeks resting upon it,

children.text: udañcatkālindīsalilasubhagaṃbhāvukaruciḥ kapolānte preṅkhanmaṇimakaramudrāmadhurimā
children.translated_text: his beauty made charming by the rising waters of the <s>Kālindī</s>, the sweetness of jeweled makara-earrings swinging at the edges of his cheeks,

children.text: vasānaḥ kauśeyaṃ jitakanakalakṣmīparimalaṃ mukundaste sākṣāt pramadasudhayā sekṣyati dṛśau ||
children.translated_text: wearing silk whose fragrance surpasses the beauty of gold, <s>Mukunda</s> himself will sprinkle your eyes with the nectar of delight.

children.text: vikadruḥ porāṇīr akhilakulavṛddho yadupater adūrād āsīno madhurabhaṇitirgāsyati tadā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vikadru</s>, ancient and eldest of the whole clan, seated not far from the lord of the <s>Yadus</s>, will sing with sweet speech,

children.text: purastād ābhīrīgaṇabhayadanāmā sa kaṭhino maṇistambhālambī kurukulakathāṃ saṃkalayitā ||
children.translated_text: while before him that hard-hearted one named terror to the cowherd women, leaning on a jeweled pillar, will relate the tale of the <s>Kurus</s>.

children.text: śilīnām uttuṃsaḥ sa kila kṛtavarmāpyubhayataḥ praṇeṣyete vālavyajanayugalāndolanavidhim
children.translated_text: That crest-jewel among warriors, <s>Kṛtavarman</s> too, on both sides, will direct the service of waving the pair of yak-tail fans.

children.text: sa jānubhyāmaṣṭāpadabhuvamavaṣṭabhya bhavitā guroḥ śiṣyo nūnaṃ padakamalasaṃvāhanarataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And, bracing himself with his knees on the golden floor, the disciple will surely be intent on massaging the lotus feet of his teacher.

children.text: vihaṃgendro yugmīkṛtakarasarojo bhuvi puraḥ kṛtāśaṅko bhāvī prajavini nideśe 'rpitamanāḥ
children.translated_text: The lord of birds, his lotus-hands joined together, will stand before him on the ground, free from fear and with his mind fixed on a swift command.

children.text: chadadvaṃdve yasya dhvanati mathurāvāsivaṭavo vyudasyante sāmasvarakalitam anyonyakalaham ||
children.translated_text: When the two wings of him resound, the resident boys of <s>Mathurā</s>, singing in Sāman tones, will set aside their mutual quarrel.

children.text: na nirvaktuṃ dāmodarapadakaniṣṭhāṅgulinakhadyutīnāṃ lāvaṇyaṃ bhavati caturāsyo 'pi caturaḥ
children.translated_text: Even the four-faced one, though clever, cannot describe the beauty of the rays from the nails of the little toes of <s>Dāmodara</s>'s feet.

children.text: tathāpi strīprajñāsulabhataralatvādahamasau pravṛttā tanmūrtistavaratimahāsāhasarase ||
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, because of the easy fickleness of a woman's understanding, I have set out upon the great daring delight of praising his form.

children.text: virājante yasya vrajaśiśukulasteyavikalasvayambhūcūḍāgrairlulitaśikharāḥ pādanakharāḥ
children.translated_text: His toenails shine, their tips ruffled by the crest of <s>Svayambhū</s>, who was distraught over the theft of the children and calves of <s>Vraja</s>.

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ yānālokya prakaṭaparamānandavirasaḥ sa devarṣir muktānapi tanubhṛtaḥ śocati bhṛśam ||
children.translated_text: After seeing them for a moment, that divine sage, his manifest supreme bliss turned tasteless, deeply pities even embodied beings who are liberated.

children.text: sarojānāṃ vyūhaḥ śriyam abhilaṣan yasya padayor yayau rāgāḍhyānāṃ vidhuramudavāsavratavidhim
children.translated_text: A mass of lotuses, longing for the splendor of his feet, undertook the painful vow of water-dwelling, full of passion.

children.text: himaṃ vande nīcairanucitavidhānavyasanināṃ yadeṣāṃ prāṇāntaṃ damanam anuvarṣaṃ praṇayati ||
children.translated_text: I bow low to the frost, which, addicted to improper procedures, brings about every year the end of life for those lotuses as punishment.

children.text: rucīnāmullāsair marakatamayasthūlakadalī kadambāhaṃkāraṃ kavalayati yasyoruyugalam
children.translated_text: By the flashes of its radiance, his pair of thighs swallows the pride of clumps of thick emerald plantain trees.

children.text: yadālānastambhadyutimavalalambe valamṛtāṃ madāduddāmānāṃ paśuparamaṇīcittakariṇām ||
children.translated_text: It became the tethering-post for the furious elephants that are the minds of the lovely cows, wild with the rut of strength's nectar.

children.text: sakhe yasyābhīrīnayanaśapharījīvanavidhau nidānaṃ gāmbhīryaprasarakalitā nābhisarasī
children.translated_text: Friend, his deep navel-lake, spread with profundity, is the source for the life of the fish that are the eyes of the cowherd women.

children.text: yataḥ kalpasyādau sanakajanakotpattivaḍabhī gabhīrāntaḥkakṣādhṛtabhuvanam ambhoruham abhūt ||
children.translated_text: From it, at the beginning of the age, arose the lotus, deep within whose chamber were held the worlds, the womb for the birth of <s>Sanaka</s>'s father.

children.text: dyutiṃdhatte yasya trivalilatikā saṃkaṭataraṃ sakhe dāmaśreṇīkṣaṇaparicayābhijñamudaram
children.translated_text: Friend, the vine of three folds on his belly bears a radiance, and that narrow belly knows the sight of rows of ropes.

children.text: yaśodā yasyāntaḥ suranarabhujaṃgaiḥ parivṛtaṃ mukhadvārāvāradvayam avaluloke tribhuvanam ||
children.translated_text: Within it <s>Yaśodā</s> beheld the three worlds, surrounded by gods, men, and serpents, with its pair of enclosing doorways being his mouth.

children.text: uro yasya sphāraṃ sphurati vanamālāvalayitaṃ vitanvānaṃ tanvījanamanasi sadyo manasijam
children.translated_text: His broad chest shines, encircled by a forest garland, at once spreading <s>Manasija</s>, the god of love, in the minds of slender women.

children.text: marīcībhir yasmin ravinivahatulyo'pi vahate sadā khadyotābhāṃ bhuvanamadhuraḥ kaustubhamaṇiḥ ||
children.translated_text: In him the <s>Kaustubha</s> jewel, sweet to the worlds, though equal to a mass of suns, always bears by its rays the appearance of a firefly.

children.text: samantād unmīladvalabhidupalastambhayugalaprabhājaitraṃ keśidvijalulitakeyūralalitam
children.translated_text: Victorious is his pair of arms, charming with bracelets shaken by the enemy of <s>Keśin</s>,

children.text: smaraklāmyadgopīpaṭalahaṭhakaṇṭhagrahaparaṃ bhujadvaṃdvaṃ yasya sphuṭasurabhigandhaṃ vijayate ||
children.translated_text: surpassing on every side the luster of pairs of pillars of opening sapphire, intent on forcibly embracing around the neck the company of gopīs faint with desire, and clearly fragrant with divine perfume.

children.text: jihīte sāmrājyaṃ jagati navalāvaṇyalaharī parīpākasyāntarmuditamadanāveśamadhuram
children.translated_text: His face holds sovereignty in the world as the full ripening of a wave of fresh loveliness, sweet with the inner joy of love's excitement,

children.text: naṭadbhrūvallīkaṃ smitanavasudhākelisadanaṃ sphuranmuktāpaṅktipratimaradanaṃ yasya vadanam ||
children.translated_text: with its creeper-like brows dancing, a playground for fresh nectar in its smile, and teeth resembling a shining row of pearls.

children.text: kimebhirvyāhāraiḥ kalaya kathayāmi sphuṭamahaṃ sakhe niḥsaṃdehaṃ paricayapadaṃ kevalam idam
children.translated_text: What need is there of these many words? Listen, friend; I shall tell you plainly this one sure mark of recognition:

children.text: parānando yasminnayanapadavībhāji bhavitā tvayā vijñātavyo madhurarava so'yaṃ madhuripuḥ ||
children.translated_text: when he has come into the path of your eyes, you must know, O sweet-voiced one, that this is <s>Madhuripu</s>, in whom supreme bliss will arise.

children.text: vilokethāḥ kṛṣṇaṃ madakalamarālīratikalā vidagdhavyāmugdhaṃ yadi puravadhūvibhramabharaiḥ
children.translated_text: If you should see <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> made artfully bewildered by the abundance of city women's coquetries, skilled in the amorous arts of intoxicated royal swan-like women,

children.text: tadā nāsmān grāmyāḥ śravaṇapadavīṃ tasya gamayeḥ sudhāpūrṇaṃ cetaḥ kathamapi na takraṃ mṛgayate ||
children.translated_text: then do not bring us village women onto the path of his hearing; a mind filled with nectar somehow does not seek buttermilk.

children.text: yadā vṛndāraṇyasmaraṇalaharīheturamalaṃ pikānāṃ veveṣṭi pratiharitam uccaiḥ kuhurutam
children.translated_text: When the pure high cry of cuckoos, causing waves of remembrance of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, surrounds every green quarter,

children.text: vahante vā vātāḥ sphuritagirimallīparimalās tadaivāsmākīnāṃ giram upaharethā murabhidi ||
children.translated_text: or when breezes blow bearing the fragrance of blossoming mountain jasmine, only then should you present our speech to the slayer of <s>Mura</s>.

children.text: purā tiṣṭhan goṣṭhe nikhilaramaṇībhyaḥ priyatayā bhavān yasyāṃ gopīramaṇa vidadhe gauravabharam
children.translated_text: In the past, while staying in the cowherd settlement, O lover of the gopīs, you placed a heavy honor upon one among all the lovely women because she was most dear.

children.text: sakhī tasyā vijñāpayati lalitā dhīralalita praṇamya śrīpādāmbujakanakapīṭhīparisare ||
children.translated_text: Her friend <s>Lalitā</s>, O graceful and self-possessed one, informs you, after bowing near the golden stool of your blessed lotus feet.

children.text: prayatnādāvālyaṃ navakamalinīpallavakulais tvayā bhūyo yasyāḥ kṛtamahaha saṃvardhanam abhūt
children.translated_text: With care you repeatedly raised from childhood one whom you nurtured with clusters of fresh lotus shoots;

children.text: cirād ūdhobhāraspuraṇagarimākrāntajaghanā babhūva praṣṭhauhī muramathana seyaṃ kapilikā ||
children.translated_text: alas, O slayer of <s>Mura</s>, this <s>Kapilikā</s> has now become a full-grown cow, her hips oppressed by the weight swelling from her long-laden udder.

children.text: samīpe nīpānāṃ tricaturadalā hanta gamitā tvayā mākandasya priyasahacarī bhāvaniyatim
children.translated_text: Near the nīpa trees, alas, you brought this <s>Vāsantī</s>, dear companion of the mango tree, to the condition of having three or four leaves.

children.text: iyaṃ sā vāsantī galadamalamādhvīkapaṭalīm iṣād agre gopīramaṇa rudatī rodayati naḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now that same <s>Vāsantī</s>, with pure streams of honey falling, weeps before us in pretense, O lover of the gopīs, and makes us weep.

children.text: prasūto devakyā muramathana yaḥ ko'pi puruṣaḥ sa jāto gopālābhyudayaparamānandavasatiḥ
children.translated_text: O slayer of <s>Mura</s>, some man was born from <s>Devakī</s>; he became the abode of the supreme joy of the cowherds' prosperity.

children.text: dhṛto yo gāndhinyā kaṭhinajaṭhare samprati tataḥ samantād evāstaṃ śiva śiva gatā gokulakathā ||
children.translated_text: But the one now held in the hard womb of <s>Gāndhinī</s> has from that time, alas, alas, caused the story of <s>Gokula</s> to set completely on every side.

children.text: ariṣṭenāhūtāḥ paśupasudṛśo yānti vipadaṃ tṛnāvartākrāntyā racayati bhayaṃ catvaracayaḥ
children.translated_text: The cowherd women, called by <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, go into danger; the line of crossroads creates fear through the invasion of <s>Tṛṇāvarta</s>.

children.text: amī vyomībhūtā vrajavasatibhūmīparisarā vahante nastāpaṃ murahara vidūraṃ tvayi gate ||
children.translated_text: These regions around the dwelling-land of <s>Vraja</s>, become like empty sky, bear pain for us, O slayer of <s>Mura</s>, now that you have gone far away.

children.text: tvayā nāgantavyaṃ kathamiha hare goṣṭhamadhunā latāśreṇī vṛndāvanabhuvi yato'bhūdviṣamayī
children.translated_text: How can you come now to the cowherd settlement here, O <s>Hari</s>? For the rows of vines on the ground of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> have become poisonous.

children.text: prasūnānāṃ gandhaṃ kathamitarathā vātanihitaṃ bhajan sadyomūrchāṃ vahati nivaho gopasudṛśām ||
children.translated_text: How otherwise could the company of cowherd women, breathing the scent of flowers carried by the wind, immediately fall into a swoon?

children.text: kathaṃ saṅgo 'smābhiḥ saha samucitaḥ samprati hare vayaṃ grāmyā nāryastvamasi nṛpakanyārcitapadaḥ
children.translated_text: How is association with us fitting now, O <s>Hari</s>? We are village women, while you are one whose feet are worshiped by royal maidens.

children.text: gataḥ kālo yasmin paśuparamaṇīsaṅgamakṛte bhavān vyagrastasthau tamasi gṛhavāṭīviṭapiniḥ ||
children.translated_text: Gone is the time when, for the sake of meeting cowherd women, you stood anxiously in the darkness beneath the trees of the house garden.

children.text: vayaṃ tyaktāḥ svāmin yadi ha tava kiṃ dūṣaṇamidaṃ nisargaḥ śyāmānāmayamatitarāṃ duṣpariharaḥ
children.translated_text: If we have been abandoned by you, master, what fault is that of yours? This is the nature of dark ones, very hard indeed to avoid:

children.text: kuhūkaṇṭhairaṇḍāvadhisahanivāsāt paricitā visṛjyante sadyaḥ kalitanavapakṣair balibhujaḥ ||
children.translated_text: birds of prey, familiar from dwelling together inside the egg until its breaking, are at once abandoned when new wings have formed.

children.text: ayaṃ pūrvo raṅgaḥ kila viracito yasya tarasā rasādākhyātavyaṃ parikalaya tannāṭakam idam
children.translated_text: This was surely the former opening act that he quickly arranged; now consider that this drama must be described according to its rasa.

children.text: mayā praṣṭavyo 'si prathamamiti vṛndāvanapate kim āho rādheti smarasi kṛpaṇaṃ varṇayugalam ||
children.translated_text: First I must ask you this, O lord of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>: do you perhaps remember the pitiable pair of syllables, '<s>Rādhā</s>'?

children.text: aye kuñjadronīkuharagṛhamedhin kimadhunā parokṣaṃ vakṣyante paśuparamaṇīdurniyatayaḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, householder of the hollows within the bowers, will the harsh fates of the cowherd women now speak in secret?

children.text: pravīṇā gopīnāṃ tava caraṇapadme 'rpitamanā yayau rādhā sādhāraṇasamucitapraśnapadavīm ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s>, expert among the gopīs and with her mind fixed on your lotus feet, has entered the path of questions suited to an ordinary woman.

children.text: tvayā goṣṭhaṃ goṣṭhītilaka kila cedvismṛtam idaṃ na tūrṇaṃ dhūmorṇāpatirapi vidhatte yadi kṛpām
children.translated_text: If this cowherd settlement, O crest-jewel of assemblies, has indeed been forgotten by you, and if the lord of smoky fleeces does not quickly show mercy,

children.text: aharvṛndaṃ vṛndāvanakusumapālīparimalair durālokaṃ śokāspadamatha kathaṃ neṣyati sakhī ||
children.translated_text: then how will my friend pass a cluster of days, hard even to look upon and now an abode of sorrow, with the fragrances of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>'s rows of flowers?

children.text: taraṃgaiḥ kurvāṇā śamanabhaginīlāghavamasau nadīṃ kāṃcid goṣṭhe nayanajalapūrairajanayat
children.translated_text: With waves that make the sister of <s>Yama</s> seem light by comparison, she has produced in the cowherd settlement a certain river from floods of tears from her eyes.

children.text: iti vāsyādveṣād abhimatadaśāprārthanamayīṃ murāre vijñaptiṃ niśamayati mānī na śamanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Murāri</s>, because of her dislike for life, arrogant <s>Yama</s> does not listen to this petition of hers, which is a prayer for the desired condition.

children.text: kṛtākṛṣṭikrīḍāṃ kimapi tava rūpaṃ mama sakhī sakṛd dṛṣṭādūrād ahitahitabodhojjhitamatiḥ
children.translated_text: Some indescribable form of yours, playing the game of attraction, was once seen from afar by my friend; her mind abandoned any awareness of harm or benefit.

children.text: hatā seyaṃ premānalam anuviśantī sarabhasaṃ pataṃgīvātmānaṃ murahara muhur dāhitavatī ||
children.translated_text: Ruined, she has rushed into the fire of love like a moth, O slayer of <s>Mura</s>, and has repeatedly burned herself.

children.text: mayā vācyaḥ kiṃ vā tvamiha nijadoṣāt param asau yayau mandā vṛndāvanakumudabandho vidhuratām
children.translated_text: What indeed can I say to you here? Through her own fault alone, that foolish one has come to desolation, O moon of the <s>Vṛndāvana</s> lotuses.

children.text: yadarthaṃ duḥkhāgnir dahati na tamadyāpi hṛdayān na yasmāddurmedhā lavamapi bhavantaṃ davayati ||
children.translated_text: For the sake of him the fire of sorrow burns her heart even now; because of him, foolish girl, she does not cast you off even by the least part.

children.text: trivakrāho dhanyā hṛdayamiva te svaṃ vapuriyaṃ samāsādya svairaṃ yadiha vilasantī nivasati
children.translated_text: Ah, <s>Trivakrā</s> is fortunate: having obtained this body of yours as if it were your heart itself, she lives here sporting freely.

children.text: dhruvaṃ puṇyabhraṃśād ajani saraleyaṃ mama sakhī praveśastatrāsīt kṣaṇam api yadasyā na sulabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Surely this straightforward friend of mine was born from a fall from merit, since even for a moment entrance there was not easily obtained by her.

children.text: kimāviṣṭā bhūtaiḥ sapadi yadi vākrūraphaṇinā kṣatāpasmāreṇa cyutamatir akasmāt kimapatat
children.translated_text: Was she possessed by spirits? Or was she suddenly struck by the serpent <s>Akrūra</s>? Did she fall all at once, her mind lost through a wounded epilepsy?

children.text: iti vyagrairasyāṃ gurubhir abhito veṇuninadaśravād vibhraṣṭāyāṃ murahara vikalpā vidadhire ||
children.translated_text: O slayer of <s>Mura</s>, when she had collapsed on hearing the sound of the flute, her elders, anxious on every side, formed such guesses about her.

children.text: navīneyaṃ sampratyakuśalaparīpākalaharī narīnarti smaraṃ mama sahacarīcittakuhare
children.translated_text: Now this new wave of the ripening of misfortune makes <s>Smara</s> dance in the cave of my companion's mind,

children.text: jagannetraśreṇī madhuramathurāyāṃ nivasataś cirādārtā vārttāmapi tava yadeṣā na labhate ||
children.translated_text: because, though you have long been living in sweet <s>Mathurā</s>, the delight of the eyes of the world, she, afflicted, receives not even news of you.

children.text: janān siddhādeśānnamati bhajate māntrikagaṇān vidhatte śuśrūṣām adhikavinaye nauṣadhividām
children.translated_text: She bows to men from places of siddhas, attends groups of mantra-practitioners, and with excessive humility renders service to physicians skilled in medicines.

children.text: tvadīkṣādīkṣāyai paricarati bhaktā girisutāṃ manīṣā hi vyagrā kimapi sukhahetuṃ na manute ||
children.translated_text: For initiation through the sight of you she worshipfully serves <s>Girisutā</s>; her distraught mind regards nothing else as any cause of happiness.

children.text: paśūnāṃ pātāraṃ bhujagaripupattrapraṇayinaṃ smarodvardvikrīḍaṃ nibiḍaghanasāradyutiharam
children.translated_text: My friend worships you, O enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, for the sake of attaining you: protector of the cows, beloved of the enemy of serpents' mount, sporting as the one who increases <s>Smara</s>, stealing the radiance of dense camphor-clouds,

children.text: sadābhyarṇe nandīśvaragiribhuvo raṅgarasikaṃ bhavantaṃ kaṃsāre bhajati bhavadāptyai mama sakhī ||
children.translated_text: always near the slope of <s>Nandīśvara</s> hill, a connoisseur of playful rasa.

children.text: bhavantaṃ saṃtaptā vidalitatamālāṅkurarasair vilikhya bhūbhaṅgīkṛtamadanakodaṇḍakadanam
children.translated_text: Heated by you, she draws you with the sap of split tamāla shoots, you who broke the battle of <s>Madana</s>'s curved bow by the bend of your brow.

children.text: nidhāsyantī kaṇṭhe tava nijabhujāvallarimasau dharaṇyām unmīlajjaḍimanibiḍāṅgī viluṭhati ||
children.translated_text: Intending to place around your neck her own creeper-like arms, she rolls upon the ground, her limbs stiff and dense with rising numbness.

children.text: kadācinmūḍheyaṃ nibiḍabhavadīyasmṛtimadād amandādātmānaṃ kalayati bhavantaṃ mama sakhī
children.translated_text: Sometimes, bewildered by the strong intoxication of dense remembrance of you, this friend of mine imagines herself to be you.

children.text: tathāsyā rādhāyā virahadahanākalpitadhiyo murāre duḥsādhā kṣaṇamapi na rādhā viramati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Murāri</s>, for <s>Rādhā</s>, whose understanding is shaped by the fire of separation, even for a moment the incurable <s>Rādhā</s> does not cease.

children.text: tvayā saṃtāpānām upari parimuktāpi rabhasād idānīm āpede tadapi tava ceṣṭāṃ priyasakhī
children.translated_text: Although you swiftly freed your dear friend from her torments before, even now she has nevertheless assumed your very behavior.

children.text: yadeṣā kaṃsāre bhidurahṛdayaṃ tvāmavayatī satīnāṃ mūrdhanyā bhidurahṛdayābhūd anudinam ||
children.translated_text: For this woman, O enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, while considering you broken-hearted, she who was foremost among faithful women has herself become broken-hearted day by day.

children.text: samakṣaṃ sarveṣāṃ nivasasi samādhipraṇayinām iti śrutvā nūnaṃ gurutarasamādhiṃ kalayati
children.translated_text: Having heard that you dwell visibly before all who love samādhi, she surely practices a very weighty samādhi.

children.text: sadā kaṃsārāte bhajasi yamināṃ netrapadavīm iti vyaktaṃ sajjībhavati yamam ālambitum api ||
children.translated_text: And because, O foe of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, you always occupy the path of the eyes of self-controlled ascetics, she is plainly making herself ready even to take hold of <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: murāre kālindīsalilacaladindīvara ruce mukunda śrīvṛndāvanamadanavṛndārakamaṇe
children.translated_text: O <s>Murāri</s>, whose splendor is like a blue lotus moving in the waters of the <s>Kālindī</s>; O <s>Mukunda</s>, jewel among the gods of love of glorious <s>Vṛndāvana</s>;

children.text: vrajānandinnandīśvara dayita nandātmaja hare sadeti krandantī parijanaśucaṃ kandalayati ||
children.translated_text: O delighter of <s>Vraja</s>, O <s>Nandīśvara</s>'s beloved one, O son of <s>Nanda</s>, O <s>Hari</s> - crying out thus constantly, she makes the grief of her attendants sprout anew.

children.text: samantād uttaptastava virahadāvāgniśikhayā kṛtodvegaḥ pañcāśugamṛgayuvedhavyatikaraiḥ
children.translated_text: Scorched all around by the flames of the forest fire of separation from you, agitated by the wounds from the huntsman with five arrows,

children.text: tanūbhūtaṃ sadyas tanuvanam idaṃ hāsyati hare haṭhādadya śvo vā mama sahacarī prāṇahariṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this thinned forest of a body, O <s>Hari</s>, will cast off today or tomorrow by force my companion's deer-like life-breaths.

children.text: payorāśisphītatviṣi himakarottaṃsamadhure dadhāne dṛgbhaṅgyā smaravijayirūpaṃ mama sakhī
children.translated_text: When my friend, who bears with a glance your beauty victorious over <s>Smara</s>, lustrous like a swelling ocean of milk and sweet as the moon with its crest,

children.text: hare dattasvāntā bhavati tadimāṃ kiṃ prabhavati smaro hantuṃ kiṃtu vyadhayati bhavāneva kutukī ||
children.translated_text: has given her heart to you, O <s>Hari</s>, how can <s>Smara</s> have power to kill her? Rather, you yourself, playful one, cause the pain.

children.text: vijānīṣe bhāvaṃ paśuparamaṇīnāṃ yadupate na jānīmaḥ kasmāttadapi bata māyāṃ racayasi
children.translated_text: O lord of the <s>Yadus</s>, you know the feeling of cowherd women; alas, we do not know why, even so, you weave illusion.

children.text: samantādadhyātmaṃ yadiha pavanavyādhiralapad balād asyāstena vyasanakulameva dviguṇitam ||
children.translated_text: If here on every side this wind-disease has babbled as a spiritual affliction, by that very force the mass of her sufferings has only been doubled.

children.text: gurorantevāsī sa bhajati yadūnāṃ sacivatāṃ sakhī kālindīyaṃ kila bhavati kālasya bhaginī
children.translated_text: The disciple of her teacher serves as minister of the <s>Yadus</s>, and this friend <s>Kālindī</s>, they say, is the sister of <s>Kāla</s>.

children.text: bhavedanyaḥ ko vā narapatipure matparicito daśāmasyāḥ śaṃsan yadutilaka yastvāmanunayet ||
children.translated_text: Who else would be known to me in the king's city, O crest-jewel of the <s>Yadus</s>, who could report her condition and entreat you?

children.text: viśīrṇāṅgīm antarvraṇaviluṭhanād utkalikayā parītāṃ bhūyasyā satatam aparāgavyatikarām
children.translated_text: Her limbs are wasting away; she is surrounded by intense longing from rolling in an inward wound, and she is constantly beset by an abundance of pallor.

children.text: paridhvastāmodāṃ viramitasamastālikutukāṃ vidho pādasparśādapi sukhaya rādhākumudinīm ||
children.translated_text: Her fragrance is ruined and all the delights of her companions have ceased. O moon, gladden the lotus of <s>Rādhā</s> even by the touch of your foot.

children.text: vipattibhyaḥ prāṇān kathamapi bhavatsaṅgam asukhaspṛhādhīnā śaure mama sahacarī rakṣitavatī
children.translated_text: O <s>Śauri</s>, somehow my companion has protected her life from calamities, held under the desire for the happiness of union with you.

children.text: atikrānte sampratyavadhidivase jīvanavidhau hatāśā niḥśaṅkaṃ vitarati dṛśau cūtamukule ||
children.translated_text: Now that the appointed day for her way of living has passed, hopeless, she fearlessly casts her eyes upon the mango bud.

children.text: pratīkārārambhaślathamatibhir udyatpariṇater vimuktāyā vyaktasmarakadanabhājaḥ parijanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Her attendants, whose minds have grown slack in beginning remedies, have given her up as one whose end is approaching and who clearly bears the torment of <s>Smara</s>.

children.text: amuñcantī saṅgaṃ kuvalayadṛśaḥ kevalamasau balādadya prāṇānavati bhavadāśā sahacarī ||
children.translated_text: Yet this lotus-eyed companion, not abandoning attachment, today preserves her life-breaths by force only through hope in you.

children.text: aye rāsakrīḍārasika mama sakhyāṃ navanavā purā baddhā yena praṇayalaharī hanta gahanā
children.translated_text: Ah, connoisseur of the rasa dance, that ever-new, deep wave of love which long ago was bound in my friend by you -

children.text: sa cenmuktāpekṣastvamasi dhig imāṃ tūlaśakalaṃ yadetasyā nāsānihitamidamadyāpi calati ||
children.translated_text: if you now are free from concern for it, then shame on this scrap of cotton, since what has been placed at her nose still moves even today.

children.text: mukunda bhrāntākṣī kimapi yad asaṃkalpitaśataṃ vidhatte tadvaktuṃ jagati manujaḥ kaḥ prabhavati
children.translated_text: O <s>Mukunda</s>, what human being in the world can tell the hundreds of unimagined things which, with wandering eyes, she somehow does?

children.text: kadācitkalyāṇī vilapati yadutkaṇṭhitamatis tadākhyāmi svāmin gamaya makarottaṃsapadavīm ||
children.translated_text: Sometimes the blessed woman laments, her mind filled with longing. I will tell that, my lord: make your way to the place of the one whose crest bears the makara.

children.text: abhūt ko 'pi premā mayi murāriripor yaḥ sakhi purā parāṃ karmāpekṣāmapi tadavalambānna gaṇayet
children.translated_text: Friend, formerly there was some love of the enemy of <s>Mura</s> for me, which, because it rested upon him, did not count even supreme expectation of action.

children.text: tathedānīṃ hā dhik samajani taṭasthaḥ sphuṭamaham bhaje lajjāṃ yena kṣaṇamapi punarjīvitum ||
children.translated_text: But now, alas, shame on it, I have plainly become indifferent; for that reason I feel shame at living again even for a moment.

children.text: garīyān me premā tvayi paramiti snehalaghutā na jīviṣyāmīti praṇayagarimakhyāpanavidhiḥ
children.translated_text: 'My love for you is very great' is only a lightening of affection; 'I shall not live' is a method for proclaiming the weight of love.

children.text: kathaṃ nāyāsīti smaraṇaparipāṭīprakaṭanaṃ harau sandeśāya priyasakhi na me vāgavasaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Why have you not come?' is a display of the sequence of remembrance. Dear friend, I have no opportunity for words as a message to <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: amī kuñjaḥ pūrvaṃ na mama dadhire kāmapi mudaṃ drumālīyaṃ cetaḥ sakhi na katiśo nanditavatī
children.translated_text: These bowers formerly gave me no joy whatever; and this row of trees, friend, how many times did it not delight my heart?

children.text: idānīṃ paśyaite yugapadapatāpaṃ vidadhate prabho muktopekṣe bhajati na hi ko vā vimukhatām ||
children.translated_text: Now look: all these at once produce burning pain. For who, when abandoned by the Lord and neglected, does not turn away?

children.text: kadā premonmīlanmadanamadirākṣī samudayāt balādākarṣantaṃ madhuramuralīkākalikayā
children.translated_text: When shall I behold the breaker of <s>Mura</s>, whose sidelong glance meets the intoxication of play, drawing me by force with the sweet warbling of his little flute,

children.text: muhurbhrāmyaccillīculukitakulastrīvratamahaṃ vilokeyaṃ līlāmadamiladapāṅgī murabhidam ||
children.translated_text: and repeatedly bewildering the vow of respectable women, which has been sipped up by his roaming eyebrows, as my eyes expand with the wine of love and desire?

children.text: yayau kālaḥ kalyāṇy adhikalitakelī parimalāṃ vilāsārthī yasminn acalakuhare līnavapuṣam
children.translated_text: Blessed one, the time has gone by, fragrant with abundant play, when that rogue, desiring dalliance, found me hidden-bodied in a mountain cave,

children.text: sa māṃ dhṛtvā dhūrtaḥ kṛtakapaṭaroṣāṃ sakhi haṭhādakārṣīdākarṣann urasi śaśilekhāśatavṛtām ||
children.translated_text: and, friend, seized me, though I had feigned deceitful anger, and dragged me by force to his breast, which was surrounded by hundreds of crescent-moon marks.

children.text: rāṇadbhṛṅgaśreṇīsuhṛdi śaradārambhamadhure vanānte cāndrībhiḥ kiraṇalaharībhirdhavalite
children.translated_text: In the forest's edge, friendly to rows of humming bees, sweet at the beginning of autumn, and whitened by waves of moonbeams,

children.text: kadā premoddaṇḍasmarakalahavaitaṇḍikamahaṃ kariṣye govindaṃ niviḍabhujabandhapraṇayinam ||
children.translated_text: when shall I make <s>Govinda</s>, beloved because of his tight arm-embrace, the elephant-driver in a love-maddened battle of passion?

children.text: mano me hā kaṣṭaṃ jvalati kimahaṃ hanta karavai na pāraṃ nāvāraṃ kimapi kalayāmy asya jaladheḥ
children.translated_text: Alas, my mind burns painfully. Ah, what shall I do? I perceive no far shore and no near shore at all of this ocean.

children.text: iyaṃ vande mūrdhnā sapadi tamupāyaṃ kathaya māṃ patāmṛṣye yasmāddhṛtikaṇikayāpe kṣaṇikayā ||
children.translated_text: I bow with my head to this: tell me at once that means by which I may endure, even for a moment, with a tiny particle of composure.

children.text: prayāto māṃ hitvā yadi kaṭhinacūḍāmaṇirasau paryātu svacchandaṃ mama samayadharmaḥ kila gatiḥ
children.translated_text: If that crest-jewel of the hard-hearted has gone away, leaving me, let him roam freely; indeed, the proper duty of my situation is my only course.

children.text: idaṃ soḍhuṃ kā vā prabhavati yataḥ svapnakapaṭādihāyāto vṛndāvanabhuvi kalān māṃ ramayati ||
children.translated_text: But who is able to bear this, since by the trick of a dream he comes here to the land of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> and delights me for a little while?

children.text: anaucityaṃ tasya vyathayati mano hanta mathurāṃ tvamāsādya svairaṃ capalahṛdayaṃ vāraya harim
children.translated_text: His impropriety torments my mind. Ah, when you reach <s>Mathurā</s>, freely restrain fickle-hearted <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: sakhi svapnārambhe punarapi yathā vibhrama madādihāyāto dhūrtaḥ kṣapayati na me kiṅkiniguṇam ||
children.translated_text: Friend, at the beginning of a dream may that rogue, coming here again through the intoxication of illusion, not waste even the string of my girdle bells.

children.text: ayi svapno dūre viramatu samakṣaṃ śṛṇu haṭhādaviśvastā mā bhūriha sakhi manovibhramadhiyā
children.translated_text: Ah, let the dream remain far away. Listen face to face: do not, friend, become too distrustful here, thinking this a delusion of the mind.

children.text: vayasyaste govardhanavipinamāsādya kutukādakāṇḍe yadbhūyaḥ smarakalahapāṇḍityamatanot ||
children.translated_text: For when your companion reached the forest of <s>Govardhana</s> in delight, he once more, unexpectedly, displayed his expertise in the battle of love.

children.text: amarṣāddhāvantīṃ gahanakuhare sūcitapathāṃ tulākoṭikvānaiścakitapadapātadviguṇitaiḥ
children.translated_text: As I ran in anger into a deep cave, the path being indicated by the doubled sound of the swinging cords, with my frightened footfalls increased twofold,

children.text: vidhīrṣan māṃ harṣottaralanayanāntaḥ sa kutukī na vaṃśīmajñāsīdbhuvi karasarojādvigalitām ||
children.translated_text: he, playful and eager to make me, whose eyes' corners trembled with joy, turn back, did not notice that the flute had slipped from his lotus hand onto the ground.

children.text: aśaktāṃ gantavye kalitanavacelāñcalatayā latālībhiḥ puṣpasmitaśavalitābhirvirudatīm
children.translated_text: Unable to go where I wished, because the edge of my new garment had been caught by creepers speckled with flower-smiles, I was crying out.

children.text: parīhāsārambhī priyasakhi sa māṃ lambitamukhīṃ prapede cumbāya sphuradadharabimbastava sakhā ||
children.translated_text: Then, beginning his jest, dear friend, your friend approached me, my face hanging down, to kiss me, his bimba-like lower lip quivering.

children.text: tato 'haṃ dhammille sthagitamuralīkā sakhi śanairalīkāmarṣeṇa bhramadaviralabhrūrudacalam
children.translated_text: Then I, friend, slowly rose up, having hidden his flute in my braided hair, with my brows moving incessantly in feigned resentment.

children.text: kacākṛṣṭikrīḍākramaparicite cauryacarite harirlabdhopādhiḥ prasabhamanayan māṃ giridarīm ||
children.translated_text: Having found a pretext in this thievish conduct, already familiar from the course of the sport of hair-pulling, <s>Hari</s> forcibly led me to the lifter of the mountain.

children.text: kadācidvāsantīkuharabhuvi dhṛṣṭaḥ sarabhasaṃ hasan pṛṣṭhālambī sthagayati karābhyāṃ mama dṛśau
children.translated_text: Once, in the cave-ground of spring, the bold one, laughing impetuously and leaning on my back, covered my eyes with both hands.

children.text: didhīrṣau jāterṣyaṃ mayi sakhi tadīyāṅguliśikhāṃ na jāne kutrāyaṃ vrajati kitavānāṃ kila guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he wished to arouse jealousy in me, friend, I do not know where this teacher of tricksters went with the tips of his fingers touching my body.

children.text: atīteyaṃ vārtā viramatu puraḥ paśya sarale vayasyaste so 'yaṃ smitamadhurimonmṛṣṭavadanaḥ
children.translated_text: This story is past; let it stop. Look before you, simple one: this is that very companion of yours, his face wiped clean by the sweetness of his smile.

children.text: bhujastambhollāsādabhimataparīrambharabhasaḥ smarakrīḍāsindhuḥ kṣipati mayi bandhukakusumam ||
children.translated_text: With the exuberance of pillar-like arms, eager for the desired embrace, that ocean of love-play throws a bandhuka flower at me.

children.text: taduttiṣṭha vrīḍāvati niviḍamuktālatikayā vadhānemaṃ dhūrtaṃ sakhi madhupurīṃ yāti na yathā
children.translated_text: So rise, bashful girl. Let us bind this rogue with a dense pearl-creeper, friend, so that he may not go to <s>Madhupurī</s>.

children.text: iti premonmīladbhavadanubhavārūḍhajaḍimā sakhīnāmākrandaṃ na kila katiśaḥ kandalayati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, stiffened by the experience of a state rising from unfolding love, does she not many times cause the crying of her friends to sprout?

children.text: aho kaṣṭ.aṃ bālyādahamiha sakhīṃ duṣṭahṛdayā muhurmānagranthiṃ sahajasaralāṃ grāhitavatī
children.translated_text: Ah, painful! From childhood I, evil-hearted, have repeatedly made my naturally simple friend grasp the knot of jealous pride here.

children.text: tadārambhādgopīgaṇaratiguro nirbharamasau na lebhe lubdhāpi tvadamalabhujastambharabhasam ||
children.translated_text: Because of that beginning, although greedy, she did not fully obtain the forceful delight of the pure pillar of your arm, O teacher of love for the host of gopīs.

children.text: alinde kālindīkamalasurabhau kuñjavasater vasantīṃ vāsantīnavaparimalodgāricikurām
children.translated_text: In the courtyard of the bower-dwelling, fragrant with lotuses of the <s>Kālindī</s>, she dwells with hair pouring out the fresh fragrance of spring jasmine.

children.text: tvadutsaṅge nidrāsukhamukulitākṣīṃ punarimāṃ kadāhaṃ seviṣye kiśalayakalāpavyajaninī ||
children.translated_text: When shall I again attend upon her, her eyes closed in the happiness of sleep in your lap, while I fan her with a cluster of tender shoots?

children.text: dhṛtānandāṃvṛndāvanaparisare śāradaniśāvilāsollāsena glapitakavarīphullakusumām
children.translated_text: Bearing joy in the region of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, her braided hair loosened and her flowers opened by the delight of autumn-night play,

children.text: tava skandhopānte vinihitabhujāvallarimahaṃ kadā kuñje līnā rahasi vihasiṣyāmi sumukhīm ||
children.translated_text: when shall I, hidden in a bower in secret, laughingly serve the lovely-faced one whose vine-like arm is placed near your shoulder?

children.text: vidūrādāhartuṃ kusumamupayāmi tvamadhunā purastīre tīre kalaya tulasīpallavamidam
children.translated_text: I am now going to fetch flowers from afar. You, meanwhile, on the bank before you, gather this leaf-shoot of <s>Tulasī</s>.

children.text: iti vyājādenāṃ viditabhavadīyasthitirahaṃ kadā kuñje gopīramaṇa gamayiṣyāmi samaye ||
children.translated_text: On such a pretext, having learned of your condition, O delight of the gopīs, when shall I spend the appointed time with her in the bower?

children.text: iti śrīkaṃsāreḥ padakamalayorgokulakathāṃ nivedya pratyekaṃ bhaja parijaneṣu praṇayitām
children.translated_text: Thus, having presented the tale of <s>Gokula</s> at the lotus feet of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, cultivate affection for each one among his attendants.

children.text: nijāṅke kādambīsahacara vahan maṇḍanatayā na yān uccaiḥ premapravaṇamanujagrāha bhagavān ||
children.translated_text: O companion of the <s>Kādambī</s>, he bore them as ornaments upon his own lap; the Lord, inclined by lofty love, favored them greatly.

children.text: miladbhaṅgīṃ haṃsīramaṇa vanamālāṃ prathamato mudā kṣemaṃ pṛcchann idamupaharethā mama vacaḥ
children.translated_text: First, O lover of the female swan, joyfully asking after the welfare of the forest garland with its meeting bends, you should present these words of mine:

children.text: ciraṃ kaṃsārāterurasi sahavāsapraṇayinīṃ kimenāmenākṣīṃ guṇavati visasmāra bhavatī ||
children.translated_text: O virtuous one, has she forgotten this doe-eyed girl, who has long loved dwelling upon the chest of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>?

children.text: idaṃ kiṃ vā hanta smarasi rasike khaṇḍanaruṣā parītāṅgī govardhanagirinitambe mama sakhī
children.translated_text: Or, alas, O connoisseur of rasa, do you remember this? My friend, her body surrounded by anger at being contradicted on the slope of <s>Govardhana</s>,

children.text: bhiyā sambhrāntākṣaṃ yadiha vicakarṣa tvayi balād gṛhītvā vibhraśyan navaśikhiśikhaṃ gokulapatim ||
children.translated_text: with frightened and bewildered eyes, here forcibly dragged the lord of <s>Gokula</s> by seizing him as his fresh peacock-feather crest slipped loose upon you.

children.text: tataḥ sambhāṣethāḥ śrutimakaramudrāmiti mudā bhavatyāṃ kartavyaḥ kimiti kuśalapraśnajaḍimā
children.translated_text: Then you should speak with delight to his earrings shaped like makaras: 'Why should there be dullness in asking after welfare with regard to you?

children.text: rucismerā yā tvaṃ racayasi sadā cumbanakalām apāṅgena spṛṣṭā sakhi murariporgaṇḍamukure ||
children.translated_text: For you, smiling with beauty, always perform the art of kissing, O friend, when touched by the sidelong glance on the mirror of <s>Murāri</s>'s cheek.

children.text: nivāsaste devi śravaṇalatikāyāmiti dhiyā prayatnāt tvāmeva praṇayahṛdayā yāmi śaraṇam
children.translated_text: Goddess, thinking that your dwelling is upon the creeper of his ear, I come to you alone for refuge with a loving heart.

children.text: parokṣaṃ vṛṣṇīnāṃ nibhṛtanibhṛtaṃ karṇakuhare hareḥ kākūnmiśrāṃ kathaya sakhi rādhāvidhuratām ||
children.translated_text: In the hollow of <s>Hari</s>'s ear, privately and very secretly, away from the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, friend, tell him with coaxing words of <s>Rādhā</s>'s wretchedness.'

children.text: parīrambhaṃ premṇā mama savinayaṃ kaustubhamaṇau bruvāṇaḥ kurvīthāḥ patagavara vijñāpanamidam
children.translated_text: O best of birds, as you respectfully embrace the <s>Kaustubha</s> jewel with love, make this petition:

children.text: agādhā rādhāyāmapi tava sakhe vismṛtirabhūt kathaṃ vā kalyāṇaṃ vahati tarale hi praṇayitā ||
children.translated_text: 'Friend, how could forgetfulness arise in you even toward unfathomable <s>Rādhā</s>? For affection, being unsteady, how indeed can it bear auspiciousness?'

children.text: muhuḥ kūjatkāñcīmaṇivalayamañjīramuralīravālambo bhrāmyadyuvatīkulagītaiḥ suramaṇe
children.translated_text: O delight of the gods, amid songs of hosts of young women, with the sounds of repeatedly ringing girdles, jeweled bracelets, anklets, and flutes as support,

children.text: sa kiṃ sākṣādbhāvī punarapi harestāṇḍavarasair amandaḥ kālindīpulinabhuvi tauryātrikabharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will that abundant mass of musicianship on the sandy bank of the <s>Kālindī</s> ever again become directly present through <s>Hari</s>'s dances filled with rasa?

children.text: navīnastvaṃ kambo paśuparamaṇībhiḥ paricayaṃ na dhatse rādhāyāḥ guṇagarimagandho 'pi na kṛtī
children.translated_text: O new conch, you have no acquaintance with the cowherd women, and not even a scent of the weight of <s>Rādhā</s>'s virtues has touched you.

children.text: tathāpi tvāṃ yāce hṛdayanihitaṃ dohadamahaṃ vahante hi klānte praṇayamavadātaprakṛtayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even so I ask you for the longing hidden in my heart; for persons of stainless nature carry affection even when they are weary.

children.text: gṛhītvā govindaṃ jaladhihṛdayānandana sakhe sukhena śrīvṛndāvanaparisare nandatu bhavān
children.translated_text: Taking hold of <s>Govinda</s>, O friend, joy of the ocean's heart, may you happily rejoice in the region of glorious <s>Vṛndāvana</s>.

children.text: kathaṃ vā te goṣṭhaṃ bhavatu dayitaṃ hanta balavān yadetasmin veṇorjayati cirasaubhāgyamahimā ||
children.translated_text: Or how could the cowherd settlement be dear to you, alas, when in it the long fortune and greatness of the flute prevails so strongly?

children.text: iti premodgārapravaṇamanunīya kramavaśāṃ parīvārān bhrātarniśamayati cāṇūramathane
children.translated_text: Thus, brother, having in order conciliated the attendants, whose minds are inclined to outpourings of love, while <s>Cāṇūra</s>'s slayer is listening,

children.text: punaḥ kopodbhinnapraṇayacaṭulaṃ tasya nikaṭe kathāmācakṣīthāḥ daśabhiravatārairvilasitām ||
children.translated_text: you should again tell near him a story, restless with affection broken open by anger, made splendid through ten avatāras.

children.text: grahītuṃ tvāṃ premāmiṣaparivṛtaṃ cittavaḍiśaṃ mahāmīna kṣipraṃ nādhita rasapūre mama sakhī
children.translated_text: O great fish, my friend, wishing quickly to seize you, a hook of her mind covered with the bait of love, in the flood of rasa,

children.text: vivekākhyaṃ chittvā guṇamatha tadagrāsi bhavatā hatāśeyaṃ kiṃ vā śiva śiva vidhātuṃ prabhavati ||
children.translated_text: cut the cord called discrimination; then, when you swallowed that, what can this hopeless woman do? Alas, alas!

children.text: varākīyaṃ dṛṣṭvā subhagavapuṣo vibhramabharaṃ tavābhyarṇaṃ bheje paramakutukollāsitamatiḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing the abundant playfulness of your handsome body, this poor girl came near you, her mind blossoming with supreme curiosity.

children.text: tirodhāya svāṅgaṃ prakaṭayasi yat tvaṃ kaṭhinatāṃ tadetat kiṃ na syāt tava kamaṭhamūrteḥ samucitam ||
children.translated_text: Since you conceal your own body and reveal hardness, is this not exactly fitting for your tortoise form?

children.text: sadā kaṃsārate sphurati ciramadyāpi bhavataḥ sphuṭaṃ kroḍākāre vapuṣi niviḍapremalaharī
children.translated_text: O enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, even now, for a long time, a wave of dense love clearly shines in your body in boar-form,

children.text: yataḥ sā sairandhrī malayaruhapaṅkapraṇayinī tvayā kroḍīcakre paramarabhasādātmadayitā ||
children.translated_text: because that perfumed woman, fond of sandal paste, was embraced by you with supreme eagerness as your own beloved.

children.text: cirādantarbhūtā naraharimayī mūrtirabhitastadīyo vyāpārastava tu na yayau vismṛtipatham
children.translated_text: Your form composed of <s>Narahari</s>, long hidden within, and his activity, have not at all gone from the path of your memory.

children.text: vinītaprahlādastvamiha paramakrūracarite prasakto yadbhūyaḥ parahṛdayabhedaṃ janayasi ||
children.translated_text: For, although you humbled <s>Prahlāda</s>, you are here attached to conduct most cruel, since again and again you cause the breaking of another's heart.

children.text: yadātmānaṃ darpādagaṇitagururvāmana mudā manorājyenāḍhyaṃ tvayi valitayā kalpitavatī
children.translated_text: When my dear friend, disregarding elders out of pride, O <s>Vāmana</s>, joyfully imagined you as herself, enriched by fantasy,

children.text: prapede tasyedaṃ phalamucitameva priyasakhī vidūre yat kṣiptā praṇayamayapāśe nigaḍitā ||
children.translated_text: she obtained just this fitting result: bound in the noose made of love, she was cast far away.

children.text: iyaṃ nātha krūrā bhṛgupatanamakaṅkṣati tato yadasyāṃ kaṭhināṃ tava samucitaṃ tadbhṛgupate
children.translated_text: Lord, this cruel girl longs for a fall from the cliff; therefore, O <s>Bhṛgupati</s>, what is hard in her is fitting for you.

children.text: asau te durbodhā kṛtiriha bhavadvismṛtipathaṃ yato jātaḥ sākṣādgururapi sa nandīśvarapatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: This deed of yours is hard to understand here, since even the lord of <s>Nandīśvara</s>, her evident guru, has entered the path of forgetting you.

children.text: nirānandā gāvaściramupasṛtā dūṣaṇakulaiḥ kharāyante sadyo raghutilaka govardhanataṭīḥ
children.translated_text: O ornament of the <s>Raghus</s>, the joyless cows, long approached by hosts of faults, at once become like asses on the slopes of <s>Govardhana</s>.

children.text: virādhatvaṃ ghoṣo vrajati bhavadīyapravasanād idānīṃ mārīcaḥ sphuṭamiha narīṇarti paritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because of your departure, the cowherd hamlet goes to the state of <s>Virādha</s>; now <s>Mārīca</s> plainly dances all around among the women here.

children.text: prasannaḥ kālo 'yaṃ punarudayituṃ rāsabhajanair vilāsinn adyāpi sphuṭamanaparādhā vayamapi
children.translated_text: O playful one, this time is favorable for rising again with those who partake of the rāsa; even now we too are plainly without offense.

children.text: vitanvānaḥ kāntiṃ vapuṣi śaradākāśavalitāṃ kṛto na tvaṃ sīradhvaja bhajasi vṛndāvanamidam ||
children.translated_text: Displaying upon your body a radiance surrounded by the autumn sky, O bearer of the plough-banner, why do you not worship this <s>Vṛndāvana</s>?

children.text: na rāgaṃ sarvajña kvacidapi vidhatte ratipatiṃ muhurdveṣṭi drohaṃ kalayati balādiṣṭavidhaye
children.translated_text: O omniscient one, he does not establish passion anywhere; again and again he hates the lord of love, and he devises hostility by force for the sake of the desired ordinance.

children.text: ciraṃ dhyānāsaktā nivasati sadā saugataratistathāpyasyāṃ haṃho sadayahṛdaya tvaṃ na dayase ||
children.translated_text: For a long time she dwells absorbed in meditation, always intent on love for the Well-gone one; yet even toward her, ah, tender-hearted one, you show no mercy.

children.text: parikleśamlecchān samadamadhupālī madhurayā nikṛntatrontapraṇayakalikākhaḍgalatayā
children.translated_text: With the sweet sword-creeper of love, cut down the mlecchas of distress, together with their intoxicated swarm of bees,

children.text: tvamāsīnaḥ kalkinniha caturagopāhitaratiḥ sadeśaṃ kurvīthāḥ pratimuditavīrādhikamidam ||
children.translated_text: and, seated here, O stainless one, delighting in the clever cowherds, make this place one that is especially gladdened by heroes.

children.text: iti premodghāṭasampuṭitavaco bhaṅgirakhilaṃ tvamāvedya klidyan mukhaparisaro locanajalaiḥ
children.translated_text: Having reported all this turn of speech, enclosed in the casket of unfolding love, while the region of your face grows wet with tears from your eyes,

children.text: tato govindasya prativacanamādhvīkapadapīmupāsīno dṛgbhyāṃ kṣaṇamavadhīthāḥ khagapate ||
children.translated_text: then, O lord of birds, waiting upon the wine-filled vessel of <s>Govinda</s>'s reply, you should hold it for a moment with your two eyes.

children.text: praṇetavyo dṛṣṭeranubhavapathaṃ nandatanayo vidheyo gopīnāṃ bhuvanamahitānāmupakṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Nanda</s> must be led onto the path experienced by the eyes; a service must be rendered to the gopīs, honored by the worlds.

children.text: iyaṃ yāmairgamyā catura mathurāpi tricaturair iti dvaidhaṃ nāntaḥ kalaya kalahaṃsīkulapate ||
children.translated_text: This clever <s>Mathurā</s> too can be reached in three or four watches of the night; therefore do not inwardly create a twofold conflict, O lord of the race of royal swans.

children.text: apūrvā yasyāntarvilasati mudā sāralarucir vivektuṃ śakyete sapadi milite yena payasī
children.translated_text: Within you there shines, with joy, an unprecedented clear brightness, by which, when milk and water are mixed, they can at once be distinguished.

children.text: kathaṃ kāraṃ yukto bhavatu bhavatastasya kṛtinā vilambaḥ kādambīramaṇa mathurāsaṅgamavidhau ||
children.translated_text: How, then, O lover of the kādambī, could delay be fitting for one as accomplished as you in arranging union with <s>Mathurā</s>?

children.text: prapannaḥ premāṇaṃ prabhavati sadā bhāgavatabhāk parācīno janmāvadhibhavarasādbhaktimadhuraḥ
children.translated_text: Some blessed one, given over to love, always strong because he has a share in the <s>Bhāgavata</s>, turned away from worldly flavor from birth and sweet with devotion,

children.text: ciraṃ ko 'pi śrīmān jayati viditaḥ śākaratayā dhurīṇo dhīrāṇāmadhidharaṇi vaiyāsakiriva ||
children.translated_text: has long been victorious on earth, renowned under the name <s>Śākara</s>, foremost among the steadfast, like the son of <s>Vyāsa</s>.

children.text: rasānāmādhārairaparicitadoṣaḥ sahṛdayair murārāteḥ krīḍāniviḍaghaṭanārūpamahitaḥ
children.translated_text: This composition, honored for taking the form of a dense arrangement of <s>Murāri</s>'s play, free from faults and resting on the supports of rasa for sensitive readers,

children.text: prabandho 'yaṃ bandhorakhilajagatāṃ tasya sarasāṃ prabhorantaḥ sāndrāṃ pramadalaharīṃ pallavayatu ||
children.translated_text: may it, belonging to that friend of all the worlds, cause a dense wave of delight to sprout within the heart of the graceful Lord.
